source.prompt: Unity game HUD sprite atlas sheet, single flat 2D graphic design asset (NOT a screenshot of gameplay, no 3D scene). Solid dark obsidian-black background (#0a0810) fills the whole canvas. Lay out exactly 16 distinct UI chrome tiles in a strict 4-column by 4-row grid of equal square cells, each tile centered and padded inside its own cell, separated by thin pure-white 3px straight grid divider lines running the full width/height so every cell boundary is unambiguous. Dark fantasy "ember and oil lantern" aesthetic matching the attached reference icons: warm ember-orange/red (#FF6B35, #FF4500) and gold (#FFD700) ornate thin metal trim for fire-themed pieces, cool sky-blue (#87CEEB) accent only where noted, painterly but clean, minimalist professional game UI chrome, no text, no letters, no digits, no gameplay art, no screenshots. Row 1 (health & oil bars): hp-bar frame + fill, oil-bar frame + fill. Row 2 (xp bar & panels): xp-bar frame + fill, meters-panel-bg, stats-panel-bg. Row 3 (skill cards & boss bar): skill-card-frame idle + ready(gold rim), boss-bar frame + fill. Row 4 (small readouts): extraction-ring frame + fill, combo-pip gem medallion, shield-readout-chip frame. Every framed tile keeps a hollow dark center so the middle can be stretched at runtime.

slicer.method: deterministic offline ImageMagick crop (grid boundaries verified against the actual PNG via numpy column/row-brightness peak detection before slicing — real dividers found at x/y ~= 0, 313, 627, 940, 1254, matching a clean 4x4 grid): per-cell inset -> -fuzz 9% -trim -> resize/pad to a fixed final size -> 4-corner floodfill-transparent against #0a0810 (same alpha-key convention already used by every other Assets/Resources/Icons/*.png, confirmed via PIL: ui-button.png corners are alpha=0).

runtime_integration.mechanism: Panel()/Bar() gained optional frameSpriteId/fillSpriteId parameters (default null, every other call site unaffected). A frame is an ADDITIVE full-stretch child (Sliced for bordered frames, Simple/flat-stretch for the two too-thin bars) drawn on top of the panel's own flat-color Image — the base color/alpha is never replaced, so every existing translucent tint and the health/oil/xp/boss 'empty track' visibility is unchanged when a sprite is missing, and still shows through the frame's hollow center when a sprite is present. A fill sprite is set directly on the existing dynamically-tinted Filled Image (health/oil/xp/boss/extraction), so all existing runtime recoloring (flash, boss-phase color swap) keeps working unmodified. Panel() also gained an out-Image overload so SkillCard() can keep a live reference to its own frame Image for the ready-state sprite swap.
runtime_integration.verification: Ran EditMode tests in an isolated git worktree (/private/tmp/hongt-head, checked out at this commit) via `Unity -batchmode -runTests -testPlatform EditMode -testResults ...` — NOT in the shared Assets/ directory, because Temp/UnityLockfile there is still held by a live interactive Editor (PID 16568) per CLAUDE.md §5; a worktree gets its own Temp/Library so the two Unity processes never touch the same lockfile or on-disk Library cache. Result: 274/276 EditMode tests passed. All 14 HudLayoutTests passed, including the two §U1 overlap graders (PhoneDungeon_SkillRow_DoesNotCoverReadouts, DesktopDungeon_SkillRow_DoesNotCoverReadouts) that specifically watch the resized shield rect, and ResetRunUi_ReseedsHealthBarForNewRun, which asserts the health bar's Image.fillAmount actually changes across a Sync() — confirming gauges still visibly animate through the new fill sprites. The 2 failures (HudIconIntegrationTests.ApplyIcon_SetsSprite_AndMaterial, .GlowShader_RendersWithoutCompileErrors) are pre-existing and unrelated: both assert a custom URP glow Material/shader compiles in batchmode ('Hidden/InternalErrorShader' / shader.isSupported == False), reproduced identically with and without -nographics, in a file (HudIconIntegration.cs, the older skill/equip/pickup icon glow system) this session never touched. A throwaway reflection-based EditMode test (not committed) additionally exercised the two behaviors that had no existing assertion coverage: the skill-card ready-frame swap (SyncDungeon at dashCooldown 1.4/0/1.4 -> frame sprite normal/ready/normal) and the shield panel's active-toggle + frame sprite/type, both passed. Visual/Play Mode confirmation in-editor or WebGL is still owed — this session verified geometry, sprite wiring, and dynamic behavior through EditMode assertions only, not a rendered screenshot.
